function: Unsupervised GruCN (GRU+CNN) outputs the precoders of a LEO satellite and UAVs and the common-rate allocation of fully distributed RSMA, maximizing weighted ergodic sum rate (pp. 9-10).
system: Downlink SAGIN: LEO satellite (2 antennas) with 2 single-antenna users and 2 UAVs (2 antennas each, 2 users each), Ka-band 28 GHz; no RIS (pp. 3, 11-12).
method: Unsupervised GruCN (2 GRU + 2 CNN layers), offline training with Adam on sampled CSIT, loss is negative weighted sum rate via sample average approximation (pp. 8-11).
data_channel: Own simulator: LEO Shadowed-Rician and UAV Nakagami-m fading with free-space loss; Ka-band, 70%/30% train/test split of generated CSI samples; no standardized or measured channel (pp. 6-7, 11).
test_conditions: Same channel distribution for training and testing (70%:30% split of generated CSI); sweeps over transmit power, users and LEO antennas, retraining not stated (pp. 9-13).
baselines: SCA (non-learned, method of [30]); learned MLP, CNN, RNN; each under FD-RSMA and under D-RSMA [50] as benchmark scheme (pp. 11-12).
metrics: Weighted ergodic sum rate (WESR), training loss, CPU processing time for precoder design (pp. 12-14).
complexity: GruCN complexity O(10ΥYZι^3) versus O((ΨKNtYZ)^3.5log(1/ε)) for interior-point optimization; CPU time about 0.4 s versus minutes for SCA (pp. 11, 13).
q1_support: p. 11: "CSI samples are generated from the channel model described in Section II" (own Shadowed-Rician LEO and Nakagami-m UAV model, pp. 6-7; no 3GPP TR 38.811 or measured data is mentioned).
q2_support: p. 9: "the distributions of the CSIT samples in both the training and testing models exhibit similarity" (70%:30% split of the same data, p. 11; the sweeps over power, users and antennas do not state a model trained in one configuration and tested in another).
q3_support: p. 12: "SCA with the same methodology and initialization in [30], (2) Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP)" plus CNN and RNN; the WESR is compared with SCA and with the learned baselines on p. 13.
q4_support: p. 11: "For each GRU layer, the computational complexity can be expressed" as O(10ΥYZι^3), versus O((ΨKNtYZ)^3.5log(1/ε)) for interior-point optimization; measured CPU time on p. 13.
q5_support: p. 11: "CSI samples are generated from the channel model described in Section II" (self-generated data; no code or data link, no public dataset and no measured data).
notes: Area 6 over 3 by precedence: the learned method designs precoders and common-rate allocation for a LEO satellite and UAVs in a SAGIN (pp. 1, 9-10). GruCN is trained unsupervised (p. 9). Shadowed-Rician and Nakagami-m statistical models are not standardized models (pp. 6-7). Borderline q2: p. 12 mentions a separate test dataset under diverse scenarios and generalization, but the paper never says a trained model is applied to a configuration absent from training; the network input and output sizes depend on the numbers of users and antennas (pp. 9-10), so each sweep point implies retraining.
